reviews_5s:
Durable, grinds great, high end functionality for not the high end price. Very easy to clean out. Sleek look.Great product, great quality, easy to use, love it.It’s a nice little devise for grinding up your “spices”. Result is kind of fluffy. Some herb will stick to the bars, not a surprise, just take a small brush and clear it out. Wouldn’t hurt to occasionally rinse with alcohol and clean it. Use this to avoid lifes little nips and cuts on fingertips. Forgot, this also does a good job working flake tobacco, cut a few half inch pieces, twist 2 or 3 times or so, let sit a bit and load up and tamp, put fire to it.The grind quality, ease of use, storage capacity is all great considering the size and price for this product. The functionality works well! I maybe wish it had a small storage compartment for the kief but it's good otherwise.We all know what you’re using it for it works very wellGrinder was large and what I was looking for. The value was also in line to what I was expecting and has held up without breaking while grinding some hard beans. Going good so farIf you’re looking for a good cheap grinder this is the one! With 3-4 turns it does the job!! It grinds the herb fairly easy. It’s the perfect size.Excellent grinder, I am actually using this for spices, not other materials. The clear construction allows you to see what you are doing and dial in the grind, you can get it very fine if you wish. I can see it degrading over time if you do a lot of harder spices, but it is very inexpensive so that is ok.

I would never use this for smokeable flower, it is way too shallow and the plastic construction would not stand up to the abuse it would face. And there is no lower chamber for kief collection - another hint this is strictly for spices.the edges on this are a little hard and not very comfortable it does grind ok (more of a coarse to medium) It is easy to clean and seems to be dishwasher safe.This is an excellently made manual herb (leave of herbs) grinder. From the ad photo, I wasn’t sure of the size. This is 3 inches across and only around 1 inch tall. This is very similar in size to the clear case for a SLR camera lens filter. Or, it’s the size of a medium women’s makeup compact. The design is well thought out. The ridges on the outer rim give you fingers something to grip. In the center of both the top and bottom lid, is a magnet so that once closed, the grinder pieces will stay together. The grinder and its internal cutting surfaces are the made from the same ultra sturdy plastic material that you would find in the clear lid of an expensive steel coffee mug.
The cutting shapes are sharp enough to tear up foliage. However, you can press your finger hard on it and you will not get cut. I placed a few dried mint leaves into the grinder. In 3 turns the leaves were broken up to an adequate degree (but not a fine grind). This worked fine for leaves. I doubt it could handle nuts or seeds or fine twigs or roots. For myself, I will use this to grinder just the very small amounts of herbs needed to finish a dish. If I needed 2 tablespoons of ground oregano leaves, I’d use a different type of grinder to get that much volume processed.
